questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have earlier studied at Humboldt University and knew the high quality of the institution. Especially, the strong focus on digital history was of interest to me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The erasmus coordination office at HU has been very helpful throughout my stay. When I have written them an e-mail with a question, mostly I have only had to wait a couple of days for answer. Also their Erasmus information webpage is really informative.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a thorough introduction session where all the necessary information was presented. Also I got information per mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had some connections in the city already and that's how I found my first room. It is difficult to find a place to stay. For Danish students, I can recommend checking out den danske kirke (Christianskirken) in Berlin. I didn't stay there, but they have some rooms for short-term rental.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I might be difficult to get Anmeldung for a short-term Zwischenmiete. This is always an issue in Berlin, and officially you are obliged to do the Anmeldung with the muncipal authorities (Bürgeramt).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As Erasmus students, we were put in front of the line. That meant that we just had to register for courses at the online agnes-platform of the university and would then be guaranteed a spot.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again we could just write the Erasmus administration office, and they would help us out.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is not much to say. It was easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level average to high. In the digital history courses the level was quite high, but for me that was perfect. I surely learned a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The teaching style was actually really different in the different courses. Some courses were very focused on exercises (e.g., the programming courses I did), whereas others were more centered around class discussion of various texts.
In comparison to UCPH, the class size was generally smaller at HU, what made in depth discussion and adjustment of the course material to the students' needs easier.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Datenmodellierung und Datenbanken für Historiker:innen
Programmieren für Historiker*innen II (Python)
Von leeren Ländern und vollen Booten. Einführung in die Migrationsgeschichte
Computer Vision für die Geschichtswissenschaften.
How to do European history? Current approaches and controversies
History of Economic Thought

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For students interested in digital history, I can warmly recommend all courses of the Lehrstuhl für Digital History (the exact course content varies between semesters).

questions.answer: It was not unexpected, but I just wanted to note that at HU you pay a admission fee of around 2000 DKK (500 per month). As part of the admission fee you get free transport in all public transport in Bundesland Berlin.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any non-academic activities of the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The only thing I know about is different .

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any non-academic activities of the university. But I would recommend people with an interest in music to check out the student symphony orchestra, the university choirs, and/or the big band.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Potsdam.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I knew german already, so it was okay for me.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would strongly recommend putting an effort into learning german before going.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like the German academic culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. You can always visit lectures (Vorlesungen), even if you don't need the ECTS. HU has a rich academic environment and a lot of interesting things are going on each semester (look for instance for the so-called Ringvorlseungen, where scholars from all over are invited to give lectures on a topic).
2. Enjoy the huge freedom you have to choose courses from a long list of options.
3. You might have to put in more work than you are used to from UCPH.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At the end of the semester, the work-load was pretty big, and I didn't have much time to do anything else in the last couple of weeks.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
